legal_issue: Whether a public authority is required to provide prior notice and an opportunity to respond before revoking a business permit in the absence of an immediate public safety emergency.
relevant_facts: A business held a valid operating permit.
A public authority revoked the permit before its expiry.
The business received no prior notice.
The business was not given an opportunity to respond.
No immediate public safety emergency was identified.

authorities.case_name: Mock Business Association v. Public Authority
authorities.relevance_to_issue: Directly establishes the requirement for reasonable notice and an opportunity to respond prior to permit revocation unless an emergency exception applies.
authorities.judicial_treatment_summary: Followed by MOCK_SC_004 on 2025-01-15 regarding general procedural fairness in permit revocation.
authorities.authority_assessment: Current and reliable good law affirming ordinary procedural fairness requirements in permit revocation proceedings.

authorities.case_name: Mock Emergency Authority v. Permit Holder
authorities.relevance_to_issue: Addresses an emergency exception permitting immediate action without a prior hearing where imminent and serious danger to public safety is shown.
authorities.judicial_treatment_summary: Distinguished by MOCK_SC_005 on 2023-02-10 for non-emergency permit revocations.
authorities.authority_assessment: Remains potentially relevant for emergency circumstances, but distinguished and inapplicable to ordinary, non-emergency revocations.

authorities.case_name: Mock Traders Union v. Licensing Board
authorities.relevance_to_issue: Previously permitted permit revocation without a prior hearing whenever administratively appropriate.
authorities.judicial_treatment_summary: Overruled by MOCK_SC_006 on 2024-06-01 regarding permit revocation without procedural safeguards.
authorities.authority_assessment: No longer good law and safe to cite is false; cannot be relied upon as legal authority.

cross_case_analysis: Across the supplied precedents, procedural requirements for permit revocation have evolved from discretionary unnotified revocation (MOCK_SC_003) to a mandatory rule of procedural fairness (MOCK_SC_001). MOCK_SC_003 has been formally overruled by MOCK_SC_006, extinguishing the legal proposition that an authority may revoke permits without a prior hearing based solely on administrative appropriateness. MOCK_SC_001 stands as good law, followed by MOCK_SC_004, establishing that a public authority must ordinarily provide reasonable notice and an opportunity to respond before revoking a permit. This standard is reinforced by Section 10 of the Mock Fair Administrative Procedure Act (MOCK_ACT_001), which requires a reasonable opportunity to be heard unless immediate action is necessary to prevent serious public danger. MOCK_CA_002 recognizes an emergency exception where credible evidence establishes an imminent danger, but this was expressly distinguished from ordinary non-emergency decisions by MOCK_SC_005.

application: Applying the combined legal authorities to the facts, the business held a valid operating permit that was revoked before expiry without prior notice or an opportunity to respond. Under MOCK_SC_001 and Section 10 of MOCK_ACT_001, prior notice and a reasonable opportunity to be heard are mandatory absent an emergency. The facts explicitly establish that no immediate public safety emergency was identified. Therefore, the emergency exception outlined in MOCK_CA_002 and Section 10 does not apply. Because the discretionary revocation rule in MOCK_SC_003 is overruled, the public authority acted contrary to the established procedural fairness requirements.
conclusion: Based on the supplied authorities, prior notice and an opportunity to respond are legally required before a public authority revokes a business permit where no emergency exception exists.
